title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 7: Major fails — good pleasure may discriminate; none disposed to glory
pass_a_gloss: Solution. The Major's consequence wavers. For it does not follow that in those things in which God acts from his mere good pleasure, he is always bound to act equally with equals: Nay on the contrary, because he acts from good pleasure, he can make a difference in the conferring of his benefits where there was no difference in the qualities or state of the persons. But what is brought first in place for confirmation of the Major, namely that with foresight of works excluded, all are equally disposed to receive the gift of election, is falsely and unskillfully asserted by Gregory. He ought to have said that all are altogether undisposed to receive glory, and disposed to undergo the pains of hell. For what disposition, that he be elected to glory, is found in him who is considered a child of wrath by nature, and contaminated with original stain?
pass_b_english: Sol. The Major's consequence fails. It does not follow that wherever God acts from mere good pleasure he must always deal equally with equals — on the contrary, because he acts from good pleasure he can discriminate in conferring his gifts where there was no difference in persons' qualities or state. And Gregory's first support for the Major — that with foresight of works excluded all are equally disposed to receive election — is false and unskillful. He should have said all are wholly undisposed to receive glory and disposed to undergo hell's pains. What disposition for election to glory is found in one reckoned a child of wrath by nature, stained with original corruption?
source_text: Sol. Vacillat Majoris consequentia. Neque enim sequitur, ut in quibus Deus agit ex mero suo beneplacito, semper aequaliter agere cum aequalibus teneatur: Imo e contra, quia agit ex beneplacito, potest discrimen facere in collatione suorum beneficiorum ubi nullum fuit discrimen in qualitatibus aut statu personarum. Quod autem affertur primo in loco ad confirmationem Majoris, scilicet Exclusa praescientia operum, omnes esse aeque dispositos ad donum electionis recipiendum, falso et imperite a Gregorio asseritur. Dicere debuisset omnes esse prorsus indispositos ad gloriam recipiendam, atque dispositos ad poenas gehennae subeundas. Quae enim dispositio, ut eligatur ad gloriam, in illo reperitur, qui naturae irae filius, et labe originali contaminatus consideratur?
